title: Sprint 6 - Aggregation Basics
description: Complete all SQL queries in this sprint.

tickets.title: Count Total Tasks
tickets.description: Find out exactly how many total tasks exist in the system.
tasks: Find out exactly how many total tasks exist in the system.
hints: Read the MySQL documentation for the specific keyword.

tickets.title: SUM, MIN, MAX, AVG
tickets.description: Find the total sum, minimum, maximum, and average of the `priority` column for all tasks.
tasks: Find the total sum, minimum, maximum, and average of the `priority` column for all tasks.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to wrap column names in parentheses.
hints: You can use multiple aggregate functions in one SELECT.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT SUM(priority), MIN(priority), MAX(priority), AVG(priority) FROM todos;

solution.query.sql: SELECT SUM(priority), MIN(priority), MAX(priority), AVG(priority) FROM todos;

tickets.title: Task Count by Status
tickets.description: Create a report showing each `status` and the total number of tasks in that status.
tasks: Create a report showing each `status` and the total number of tasks in that status.
common_mistakes: Selecting non-aggregated columns without GROUP BY.
hints: Read the MySQL documentation for the specific keyword.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS task_count FROM todos GROUP BY status ORDER BY status;

solution.query.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS task_count FROM todos GROUP BY status;

tickets.title: Overloaded Users
tickets.description: Show the `user_id` and count of tasks only for users who have strictly more than 5 tasks.
tasks: Show the `user_id` and count of tasks only for users who have strictly more than 5 tasks.
common_mistakes: Using WHERE instead of HAVING for aggregates.
hints: Read the MySQL documentation for the specific keyword.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS total_tasks FROM todos GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY user_id;

solution.query.sql: SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS total_tasks FROM todos GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;
